DEC-001.rationale: Milestone v2.18: converged DistributedReduce/AllGather/Broadcast onto the verified NCCL layer in v2.17 but deliberately deferred MeshBarrier, the last high-level distributed op still on the legacy per-instance host-event-poll path (barrier.cu, non-threadsafe barriering_ flag, cross-thread cudaEventQuery polling; no real per-rank multi-GPU test — NoDeadlock runs single-host-thread). The R15-R17 pattern is that every never-run multi-GPU surface has hidden real bugs, and MeshBarrier multi-GPU is now effectively never-run (only the single-GPU tests exercise it; the event-poll loop has never been driven from real per-rank threads). Plan: (P1) build a real thread-per-rank multi-GPU MeshBarrier test (synchronize + synchronize_devices driven concurrently per rank) to expose defects and gather evidence; (P2) converge MeshBarrier onto the verified NcclBarrier layer (current_comm routing, sync/async preserved, single-GPU fallback kept) and flip the new tests on; (P3) distributed-ops harness robustness — isolate the tracked harness flake (issue-v17-dist-ops-harness-flake) and the R16 review HIGH-B shared-NcclContext poisoning if a rank exits a collective early (readiness/fault exchange hardening).
DEC-001.alternatives_rejected: Skipping MeshBarrier and closing the milestone (it is the last unconverged v1.1 primitive and its multi-GPU path has never been genuinely exercised); converging barrier.cu wholesale before writing the per-rank test (the P1 evidence-driven flow worked for the three data ops in v2.17); opening a deep-dive milestone instead (the two open issues and the MeshBarrier gap scope this milestone more tightly).

DEC-003.title: Milestone v2.19 direction: verify + converge neural parallel-training surfaces (TensorParallelMatmul, SequenceParallel) onto the verified real-multi-GPU layer
DEC-003.rationale: v2.15-v2.18 converged and verified every high-level distributed op on the verified NCCL layer (distributed ops, distributed matmul, MeshBarrier) - RIL graph now has zero active tasks. The largest remaining never-run multi-GPU surface is the neural parallel-training layer: TensorParallelMatmul multi-GPU execution has no real multi-GPU test (tests/neural/tensor_parallel_test.cpp checks only buffer-size formulas and profiler math), and SequenceParallel tests pass comm=nullptr so they never drive a real NCCL collective. Static read of src/cuda/neural/tensor_parallel_matmul.cpp shows strong bug smells: ColumnParallel partitions B/C as contiguous slices (column-major semantics) while RowParallel slices A as contiguous rows (row-major), the SAME matrix order cannot satisfy both, recv_buffer is dead code, every rank redundantly computes ALL slices with the full B buffer, local_n = n/tp_degree drops remainders, and there is no divisibility guard. The R15-R18 pattern is that every never-run multi-GPU surface hides real bugs, so this path is expected RED. Plan: (P1) real thread-per-rank multi-GPU execution tests vs single-GPU reference (RED evidence); (P2) correct the partition/layout math on the verified NCCL layer and prove numerical equivalence; (P3) drive SequenceParallelAttention gather/scatter/all-reduce with a real NcclContext communicator, then optionally scale to 4/8 GPUs (host has 8x A100).
DEC-003.alternatives_rejected: MPI enablement is env-bound (no MPI headers on host); inference-layer multi-GPU (FlashAttention/PagedAttention) is a larger follow-up that depends on the sequence-parallel verification here; pure 8-GPU scale-up of already-green suites adds confidence but no new verified surface.

DEC-007.title: v2.21 milestone direction: real weight-managed TensorParallelLayers (Megatron weight-shard semantics)
DEC-007.rationale: TASK-010 is the only active high-priority task: the v1.3 layer wrappers own no weights and forward() throws (DEC-006 fail-fast disposition). To close them we implement true weight-sharded layers: ColumnParallelLayer holds per-rank column shard [k x out/tp] (forward = local shard matmul -> sharded output, no comm); RowParallelLayer holds per-rank row shard [k/tp x n] (forward = local matmul on sharded input + block AllReduce -> replicated output); TensorParallelMLP = SiLU-gated FFN (gate/up ColumnParallel, down RowParallel). This is the only semantics that keeps the layer stack coherent (header docs match: col shards output, row consolidates to full width) and actually achieves weight sharding. Rank resolved via ctx.rank_of_device (v2.20 verified convention); per-instance stream-bound cuBLAS handle for thread-per-rank safety; shape rejection on non-divisible dims; single-GPU full-weight reference parity is the acceptance gate (v2.19/v2.20 pattern). API changes (explicit in_features/out_features instead of rigid 3*hidden_dim QKV) are safe: zero callers in the tree. Multi-commit diff exceeds the 300-line default because it replaces a stub surface + adds tests + a silu_and_mul kernel; exception documented per skill rule 8.
DEC-007.alternatives_rejected: Keeping fail-fast (leaves dead surface); re-exposing the TensorParallelMatmul primitive with replicated full weights only (defeats weight sharding and cannot compose a coherent MLP: the verified RowParallel primitive is batch-split, not weight row-parallel); leaving the v1.3 3*hidden_dim QKV-only column API (too rigid for the MLP gate/up).

DEC-010.alternatives_rejected: End-to-end TensorParallelAttention composition (fold all heads; heavier geometry, more integration harness than capability — remains the later capstone); device-native fused optimizer kernels (a performance task, orthogonal to the correctness milestone here; the existing host-side AdamW is sufficient and independently verified); a full autograd/DAG framework (too broad; reference-parity of one training step is the immediate need).

DEC-012.rationale: v2.21-2.25 delivered weight-sharded layers, backward passes, a device CE-loss seed, per-shard AdamW stepping, and a MicroTrainer that provably converges on the parallel stack — but every model trained so far is a plain MLP; no attention exists on the tensor-parallel path (the single-GPU MultiHeadAttention is an incomplete shell, issue-v24-mha-incomplete). Attention is the piece that turns the trainable stack into a trainable transformer. The design reuses the verified conventions: QKV as ColumnParallelLayer (each rank owns contiguous head columns, no comm in forward), output as RowParallelLayer (one block-wise AllReduce), multi-head SDPA (QK^T/sqrt(d), softmax, V) as new kernels with full analytic backward (dQ/dK/dV via the standard scaled-dot-product chain); backward follows the v2.23 pattern (per-rank shard grads, col-layer grad-input AllReduced).
DEC-012.alternatives_rejected: Device-native fused AdamW kernels (a performance task, orthogonal to capability; deferred); a full mini-language-model milestone (needs the attention block first — attention is the dependency, so it is this milestone); reusing the incomplete single-GPU MultiHeadAttention (fixing it is only single-GPU; the milestone is the TP path).
